title: Euler characteristic of an invertible twist on an integral proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $\xi$ be the generic point, characterized by $\overline{\{\xi\}}=C$. Its local ring is the residue field $\mathcal O_{C,\xi}=\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Set $r=\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\mathcal F_\xi$, the finite dimension of the generic stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk, def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. For the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle],
$$\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal F)=r\deg_k(\mathcal L)+\chi(C,\mathcal F).$$
The generic rank $r$ may be zero; no local freeness of $\mathcal F$ or smoothness of $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, specialization to an invertible first factor (n=1).

proof.text: Fix $\mathcal L$ and put $r(\mathcal H)=\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\mathcal H_\xi$ and $D(\mathcal H)=\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H)-\chi(C,\mathcal H)-r(\mathcal H)\deg_k\mathcal L$. By [lem-trf-curve-euler-defect-additivity], $C$ is Noetherian, these tensors are coherent, all generic ranks are finite, $D(0)=0$, and $D$ is additive on coherent short exact sequences. Thus the property $\mathcal P(\mathcal H):D(\mathcal H)=0$ holds for zero and satisfies two out of three: if two of the integers in $D(\mathcal H_2)=D(\mathcal H_1)+D(\mathcal H_3)$ vanish, the third does. An isomorphism of coherent modules induces inverse maps on their generic stalks, tensors and cohomology groups; their dimensions, Euler characteristics and hence $D$ agree. Thus $\mathcal P$ is invariant under isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, condition (1) and zero-object preliminary.

proof.text: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ be an integral closed subscheme with generic point $z$. By [lem-trf-curve-integral-closed-tests], either $Z=C$ over $C$, or $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ over $C$ for a closed $z\ne\xi$. In the first case that same lemma supplies the coherent witness $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_C$, with support $C$, generic stalk killed by $\mathfrak m_\xi$, and residue-field dimension one. Its tensor Euler difference is $\deg_k\mathcal L$, so $D(\mathcal G)=\deg_k\mathcal L-1\deg_k\mathcal L=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, condition (2), integral closed subscheme dichotomy and Z=X.

proof.text: In the closed-point case let $j:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow C$ be the canonical residue-field inclusion. By Step 2 its image is the underlying closed subset of $Z$. Apply [lem-trf-curve-closed-point-twist-witness] to $j$: the witness $\mathcal G=j_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)}$ is coherent with support $\{z\}=|Z|$, and $\mathcal G_z$ is killed by $\mathfrak m_z$ and has residue-field dimension one. The lemma also gives $\mathcal G_\xi=0$ and $\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal G)=\chi(C,\mathcal G)$. Hence $D(\mathcal G)=0-0\deg_k\mathcal L=0$. These are the four witness conditions for the underlying closed subset $|Z|$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, condition (2), reduced closed point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-coherent-property-devissage] with $X=C$ and $\mathcal P(\mathcal H)$ defined by $D(\mathcal H)=0$. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity and conditions (0) and (1). For each integral closed $Z$ with generic point $z$, Steps 2-3 supply a coherent $\mathcal G$ satisfying (2)(a) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=Z$, (b) $\mathfrak m_z\mathcal G_z=0$, (c) $\dim_{\kappa(z)}\mathcal G_z=1$, and (d) $D(\mathcal G)=0$. Here $z=\xi$ for $Z=C$, while for a closed point $z\ne\xi$ the dimension-one stalk is at $z$ and its rank at $\xi$ is zero. The cited theorem therefore gives $D(\mathcal F)=0$. Rearranging yields $\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal F)=r\deg_k\mathcal L+\chi(C,\mathcal F)$, including $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, final application of coherent-lemma-property (01YI).

lean.statement: theorem eulerChar_tensor_invertible_generic_rank (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Scheme.{u}) [C.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C] [IsProper (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (L : C.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (F : C.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace F) (ξ : C) (hξ : closure ({ξ} : Set C) = Set.univ) : (L ⊗ F).eulerChar k = (Module.finrank (C.presheaf.stalk ξ) (F.presheaf.stalk ξ) : ℤ) * L.degree k + F.eulerChar k
